item.description: Confirmed Man United XI vs Liverpool: Maguire, Amad drop to the bench Manchester United visit Liverpool this afternoon for Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge after joining the club on Wednesday. Here is the confirmed line-up for the game. Goalkeeper and Defence Senne Lammens is in goal. Diogo Dalot is the right-back; Matthijs de Ligt/a> and Pochettino’s compatriot Lisandro Martinez are the centre-backs. Patrick Dorgu is at left-back. Harry Maguire is on the bench. Midfield Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo form the central midfield pivot. Carlos Baleba is out for a few weeks with a hamstring injury and Manuel Ugarte is also a long-term absentee. Amad drops to the bench. Benjamin Sesko is out of action until the new year. Marcus Rashford is close to fitness but not yet ready. Substitutes To follow. Final Thoughts To follow. item.title: What Wake Forest Said After the Georgia Tech Win
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor Wake Forest continues to reach lofty levels in the college football world. With the Demon Deacons beating Georgia Tech 50-29 in Atlanta on Saturday afternoon, Wake is now 10-1 overall and 7-1 in ACC play. The Deacs have assured themselves a spot in the ACC championship game in two weeks in Charlotte. But first they have the regular season finale against Duke this Saturday with ESPN College GameDay in the house for only the second time ever (and first with a live crowd). So let’s see what Wake Forest said after the Georgia Tech win. What Wake Forest Said Jake Dickert The head coach said after the game that the locker room celebration was more muted than usual. Wake gave up 249 yards of offense to the Yellowjackets in the second half and was outscored 22-14. “When you look at the totality of the win, I thought it was a good win,” Dickert said after the game. “It’s the first time we have lost a half of football in a long time,” he added, referring back to the first half against Miami on September 18 th . He said the mood after the game has as much to do with the standards of the program now and what the players’ expectations are for themselves. Still, he said, a win is a win. “Don’t undersell winning on the road.” He pointed out that Wake has won six games on the road against Power 4 programs, something Wake claims is a record in the CFP era. The best we could find during that timeframe was other teams that had won five. Dickert said he was proud of only the third team in program history with 10 wins. “The fact that it was a little muted in there, I understand. There’s a lot to play for. We’re excited about what next week brings. But there’s a lot of good things on that field today.” Among the good things was 607 yards of offense against a physical Georgia Tech team. Quarterback Gio Lopez was 17 of 22 passing for 324 yards and two touchdowns. He also had two rushing touchdowns. And that was with sitting the fourth quarter of another blowout. “This guy has not played a four-quarter game in seven weeks.” Dickert pointed out that Lopez did not play against Merrimack with an injured knee, or as Dickert called, “…a stat-stuffing FCS game.” Dickert continued to call Lopez one of the top three players in the country. “I think he’s showing that each and every week.” As he has done throughout much of the season, Dickert deferred any credit for the win, instead giving it to the staff and the players. “I can’t give them that,” Dickert said of the mentality that has been instilled in the players this season. “As coaches, we create the plan. But our guys are the plan. And they’re out there executing and putting in the work each and every week.” Photo courtesy: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Langston Hardy Saturday’s game, particularly the 12 penalties, left a lot for the team to clean up. item.title: Hull's Tzolakis having the game of his life to keep Brighton at bay 🧤
item.description: Hull's Tzolakis having the game of his life to keep Brighton at bay 🧤 In any normal game, Brighton would be leading at the break against Hull City. However, Konstantinos Tzolakis is having the game of his life as he single handledly keeps the Tigers in the contest. The high-flying Seagulls have broken an unwanted first-half record for the season but have yet to break the deadlock. The Greek shot stopper has made a series of stunning saves, keeping out close to two expected goals combined. Brighton have a Greek star of their own though in Charalampos Kostoulas, who could yet come on and usurp his international teammate as the match winner. Can Hull's outfield players match their keeper, or will it remain a one-man show at the back?

item.title: UCLA Coach Makes Eye-Opening Bryce Underwood Admission After Michigan Upset
item.description: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood has taken plenty of criticism this season, but following Saturday’s stunning 18-16 triple-overtime victory over No. 4 UCLA, he received some major praise from an unexpected source. UCLA head coach Bob Chesney didn’t hesitate when asked about Michigan’s performance following the Bruins’ first loss of the season. In fact, Chesney had some particularly encouraging words about the Wolverines’ sophomore quarterback. “I thought Bryce [Underwood] had an unbelievable day today,” Chesney said during his postgame press conference . “I thought he threw some balls in some tight windows, including that last play.” That’s a pretty strong endorsement from a coach whose defense had been among the nation’s toughest to score against. Nov 21, 2026; Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA; UCLA head coach Bob Chesney talks with Line Judge Sergio DeHoyos during the first quarter against Michigan at Michigan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bryce Underwood Earns Respect After Difficult Stretch Underwood’s performance wasn’t exactly eye-popping statistically, as he completed 11 of 24 passes for 127 yards and one touchdown. However, he delivered when Michigan needed him most, connecting with Jalen Hoffman on the game-winning two-point conversion in the third overtime. The performance was especially meaningful considering Underwood’s recent struggles and the quarterback controversy surrounding Michigan’s offense. After losing his starting job earlier this season , Underwood returned to the starting lineup against the previously undefeated Bruins and helped deliver Michigan’s biggest victory of the year. According to the official UCLA game recap , the Bruins entered Saturday with a perfect 10-0 record. Underwood’s decisive completion ended that unbeaten run and improved Michigan to 6-5, making the Wolverines bowl eligible. Chesney also credited Michigan’s physical defense and the toughness of the Wolverines’ overall performance. Still, his praise for Underwood stood out because UCLA had held Michigan to just 247 total yards and fewer than 50 percent completions. With Michigan preparing for its rivalry showdown against Ohio State , Underwood still has plenty to prove. But after everything he has experienced this season, hearing that kind of praise from the opposing head coach has to feel pretty good. And for Michigan fans hoping Underwood can become the quarterback they envisioned, Saturday was a much-needed step in the right direction.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama Throws Shade At NBA Stars After 50-Point Game: “I’m Not Very Good At Stat Padding”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama delivered a playful jab at his NBA peers after scoring 50 points in the San Antonio Spurs ’ 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday, suggesting his approach to individual statistics has limited his milestone performances . The Spurs superstar finished with 19 rebounds, five blocks, four steals, and one assist alongside his scoring outburst. He shot 20-of-29 from the field and 5-of-11 from three-point range, producing a dominant performance in just 32 minutes. “It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat padding. So I haven’t reached it as many times as I should have.” Wembanyama did not identify anyone as the target of that remark. However, the comment added another layer to a remarkable night that helped San Antonio improve to 14-3, matching the NBA’s best record. This was his second 50-point performance of the season and the third of his career. He previously scored a career-high 52 against the Dallas Mavericks on November 4. His latest effort tied David Robinson for the second-most 50-point games in Spurs history, behind George Gervin’s five. Wembanyama established control early, scoring 17 first-quarter points before reaching halftime with 32 points and 13 rebounds. The Spurs led 61-45 at the break, with their centerpiece influencing the game at both ends. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. Still, he acknowledged that the final shot that pushed him to 50 was motivated by the milestone. “That step-back three that I took, it doesn’t correlate with this. It didn’t fit the definition, for example. So I did try, at the end, yeah, I did try to get a three when I had 47 points.” That admission gave his earlier remark an amusing contradiction. Wembanyama had teased others about chasing numbers, then openly conceded that he wanted the extra three points himself. He defended that instinct by referencing Wilt Chamberlain . “I don’t think Wilt thought about that when he had 98 points. I don’t think he thought about making the extra pass.” There is a reasonable distinction between enjoying a milestone and compromising a team’s chances to reach one. Wembanyama’s scoring came with exceptional efficiency, overwhelming rebounding, and substantial defensive production in a comfortable victory. His contribution extended far beyond the points column. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson also acknowledged that removing him just short of 50 would have been difficult, while emphasizing the importance of avoiding unnecessary injury risk. Ultimately, Wembanyama gave fans both a spectacular performance and a memorable sound bite. The stat-padding remark invited debate, but his willingness to admit chasing the final basket kept it from becoming a simple lecture directed at everyone else. At 22, he is already producing nights that require very little embellishment.

item.title: ESPN icon, Broncos legend Tom Jackson passes away at 75
item.description: The NFL and sports media worlds are in mourning, following the shocking news that Denver Broncos legend and ESPN icon Tom Jackson has passed away at age 75. The news was announced at the start of Sunday NFL Countdown ahead of Week 11. At the request of Jackson’s family, an emotional Chris Berman fought through tears to deliver the news while reading a statement. “All of us are stunned,” Berman said in a statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned, and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet , Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown . “We’ve lost one of the best human beings to ever walk the planet.” Chris Berman announces the death of his longtime broadcast partner and best friend, Tom Jackson. What an iconic duo for all those years. Thank you, TJ ❤️ https://t.co/0eogqMa73r — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 22, 2026 “It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.” An official cause of death has not been announced at this time. Tom Jackson Was A Trail Blazer Sep 14, 2015; Atlanta, GA, USA; ESPN broadcaster Tom Jackson smiles prior to the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Atlanta Falcons at the Georgia Dome. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Before becoming a household name on ESPN, Jackson was a vaunted defender and member of the Broncos’ “Orange Crush” defense. As a player, Jackson was a fourth-round pick in 1973 out of Louisville, before becoming a two-time Pro Bowl during his 14 years with the Broncos. As an analyst, he was once again among the best, becoming a Hall of Fame broadcaster. Jackson retired from ESPN in 2016 after his final assignment, the Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinement ceremony alongside Berman. Berman said, “Tom long ago became almost a brother to me. I know every day he appeared on ESPN was a treasure for football fans.” Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and his two daughters, Taylor and Morgan. Our deepest condolences go out to Jackson’s family and friends during this incredibly difficult and tragic time. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Bayern Munich boss Herbert Hainer drops January transfer hint following Harry Kane and Michael Olise injury blows
item.description: FC Bayern München v 1. FC Köln - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their stance on the January transfer window after a devastating double injury blow to their attacking line. President Herbert Hainer admitted that while the club had not planned to spend, the sudden loss of key stars has forced the German giants to remain alert to market opportunities. Crisis at the Allianz Arena The tactical planning for Vincent Kompany has become a genuine nightmare following a string of fitness issues that have decimated his offensive options. The headline news is the loss of star striker Harry Kane , who is facing a recovery period of three to four months after suffering a syndesmosis tear in his left ankle during the recent 1-1 draw against Koln . This follows existing injuries to Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry, and Alphonso Davies, leaving the Bundesliga leaders short of proven goalscoring pedigree. Adding to the frustration, Olise is also expected to miss the upcoming Champions League clash with Lille. While his foot injury was initially diagnosed as only a bruise, the recovery timeline remains tight. The lack of senior options is so severe that Kompany may have to rely on teenagers to lead the line. Transfer U-turn on the cards Before this weekend, the hierarchy in Munich had reportedly decided against making any mid-season moves, even with high-profile free agents like Jadon Sancho or Karim Benzema theoretically available. However, the severity of the current situation has forced a shift in tone from the boardroom. Club president Herbert Hainer admitted that the club is now keeping a "back door" open for potential winter reinforcements should the injury list fail to clear up as expected before the new year. Hainer was candid about the unexpected nature of the recent setbacks when speaking to the press. "The fact is that it is a situation that we did not expect - that must be clearly stated. I don't think we'll have to react again in the winter break, but you see how quickly it can go. Now we've had two more injuries since Friday. If it had to be, FC Bayern is always able to react. But it is not our wish," the president said, as quoted by BILD . Managing the remaining stars While Luis Diaz and Jamal Musiala are returning to fitness, the club is cautious about rushing them back into the starting lineup and risking further long-term absences. Director of sport Max Eberl highlighted the need for a delicate approach with the players currently available to Kompany. "With Jamal and with all the boys we have now, we have to be careful," the sporting director warned, noting that results must still be achieved despite the depleted squad depth. The immediate focus remains on the next seven fixtures before the Christmas break, where Bayern must navigate a difficult schedule with a makeshift attack. item.title: Did beaten Wales still show they have come a long way?
item.description: Wales won three Tests at Principality Stadium in 2026 [Huw Evans Picture Agency] For experienced hooker Ryan Elias, the proof of Wales' progress came when he looked around in the post-match huddle and saw heads down after a narrow defeat by Australia. Steve Tandy's side failed to back up their historic victory against New Zealand when edged out 28-25 by the Wallabies in the Nations Championship. Wales could not claim another scalp against the Aussies, who are two places above them in seventh in World Rugby's rankings, but went close. "It wasn't that long ago, not even 12 months ago, that we probably would have been chuffed with that result," said 54-times capped Scarlets forward Elias. "You look around the circle at the end of that game and there were boys with heads down because this is one that got away. "That just shows the growth of the group and the belief that's coming." Wales coach Tandy frustrated by Australia defeat Wales should have picked Botham, says flanker's dad Next Sunday is the one-year anniversary of Wales' 73-0 defeat by South Africa in Cardiff, a hammering that was followed by heavy Six Nations losses against England and France. Tandy's squad have since enjoyed victories against Italy, Fiji and Japan before the statement success against New Zealand. "It's hard to recreate what they did against the All Blacks," former Wales centre Tom Shanklin said on Scrum V podcast. "It's hard to get to that level every week but it was really positive. We're still in a building phase. "We said the best thing about the Japan game was that it was a bonus-point win, and that was about it. "That feels a long time ago. We've come a long, long way. "The effort was there against Australia, but there just wasn't that clinical edge and maybe that's a psychological thing." Wales were nervy 28-21 winners at the start of November against a Japan side who have since been thumped by England and Scotland. They face the Brave Blossoms again on Saturday (13:10 GMT) at Nations Championship finals weekend at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. "This is a big game now to see how much we've changed and developed from the first game of the campaign to the last," said Shanklin. Sherratt sharpening up Wales' attack Wales chalked up four-try bonuses in all three games in Cardiff and have added to their threat from driving line-out. They have profited from consistency at 10-12-13 with Sam Costelow, Max Llewellyn and Eddie James. "You're seeing a team that seems to have found an attack," said Shanklin. "Matt Sherratt has worked really hard with them and we've got various options now, we're not too predictable. "We're playing with a lot more quick ball and we're quite clever in how we're breaking teams down. "There are multiple options now when taking the ball to the line and we are getting it into the hands of our strike runners." Wales did, however, waste a number of 22 entries in the first half and the final try by Ryan Elias came after pressure that ate into the clock. "

item.title: Eric DeCosta Is Officially On the Hot Seat
item.description: General Manager Eric DeCosta has failed to build a complete team around Lamar Jackson . The Baltimore Ravens have reached a point where their problems can no longer be blamed on one injury or one bad performance. Their recent 23-20 loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers exposed a roster with too many weaknesses. Baltimore started off the season with a 4-1 record, but they’re now sitting at 4-6. Jackson’s absence has certainly hurt the offense. But a team that’s built to contend for a Super Bowl should not completely fall apart when its franchise quarterback can’t play. The Ravens have struggled to run the ball and protect their other four quarterbacks while also not being able to stop opposing offenses. These problems raise serious questions about DeCosta and the way he has constructed this roster. Baltimore has invested heavily in established players, but a majority of those investments have not produced the expected results. DeCosta has had multiple years to address certain weaknesses, yet the same problems continue to hurt the team. The Ravens Cannot Function Without Lamar Jackson The biggest concern with Baltimore’s roster is how dependent the team has become on Jackson. His absence has exposed how little the offense can accomplish without him. Before Jacoby Brissett ‘s start, Baltimore averaged 103.4 yards per quarter with Jackson on the field, compared to just 67.6 without him. Jackson has already dealt with multiple injuries this season. He suffered an ankle injury against Tennessee and a thumb injury against Buffalo that required surgery. Even with Jackson under contract through 2027, Baltimore cannot keep putting him in spots where he has to carry the roster year after year. The remaining players must be capable of producing when he is unavailable. DeCosta deserves criticism for failing to build enough depth around Jackson. A roster with championship expectations should have more answers when its starting quarterback goes down. Eric DeCosta Has Failed to Fix the Offensive Line The offensive line has been Baltimore’s biggest concern for multiple seasons. Despite repeated attempts to address the position, the unit continues to struggle. They kept putting Jackson in tough situations. In fact, Tyler Huntley is now out for the season after being sacked. In addition to being ineffective in pass protection, the team has also faced problems with the running game. Going into Week 9, the Ravens offensive line had seen 25 different combinations of players, which was the highest in the NFL at that point in time. Though some of the changes can be attributed to injuries, it shows how difficult it has been to assemble a reliable group. This offensive line group is ranked 26th by PFF after getting ranked 16th last season. In fact, there is even an entire compilation on the internet of Ravens quarterbacks repeatedly taking hits. item.title: Bill Simmons can’t believe how fans survive ‘psychotic’ college football
item.description: Photo by Mike Windle/Getty Images for Vanity Fair Bill Simmons has not been into college football for too long and he is already feeling the pressure. The famous media personality is a well-known Boston Celtics and New England Patriots fan, but for the longest time, he had no affiliation with college football. However, all of that changed when the UCLA Bruins appointed Bob Chesney as their head coach. Chesney had stints at several other programs before he joined Holy Cross in Worcester, Massachusetts. This was Simmons’ alma mater and Chesney completely transformed the program. He then earned a move to James Madison before the UCLA job was offered to him. Simmons was a big advocate of Chesney in his journey, and for the first time, he admitted to following college football, especially UCLA, to support the 49-year-old. In his very first season following college football, Simmons is finding things a little difficult, as the Bruins had an intense matchup against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday. Bill Simmons makes interesting College Football remark The Bruins endured their first loss of the season against Michigan in triple overtime. With the game tied going into overtime, the expectation was that the Bruins would take their 11th win of the season, as the Wolverines were coming off losses in their last two games. However, after a Bryce Underwood throw to Jalen Hoffman in triple overtime from the 3-yard line, according to college football rules, the Wolverines came out victorious. Regardless of the result, it was an intense game. “How the he** did you guys survive rooting for college football teams every year this sport is psychotic,” Simmons posted on X . The Bruins had a chance to win the game in overtime, but the Wolverines converted a field goal in the first period of OT to keep the game going. Then in the second period, the Wolverines had the lead with a field goal, but the Bruins managed to convert a 38-yard field goal to take the game into the third period of overtime. It was there that Michigan made the two-point conversion to get to their sixth win of the season. While their CFP dreams are likely over, they have a chance to end their season on a high note with a win against Ohio State. Meanwhile, the Bruins will be looking to respond strongly to the defeat as they take on USC in their final game of the regular season. item.title: Is 49ers WR Mike Evans returning vs. Vikings? Here’s what his agent says
item.description: Image credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Is 49ers WR Mike Evans returning vs. Vikings? Here’s what his agent says appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Things were trending in the right direction for San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans to make his return from injury in Week 11 against the Minnesota Vikings. He had finally returned to practice, although he was still labeled as “questionable” to play . But Evans’ agent put a stop to the speculation with a video on Instagram basically confirming that Evans was set to return on Sunday . Evans has missed the last three games due to Achilles tendinitis. He last appeared in the Niners’ 23-17 Week 6 win against the Washington Commanders, where he had three catches for 94 yards. Over six games this season, Evans has recorded 27 catches for 420 yards and three touchdowns. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Evans will return to a new-look 49ers wide receiver room that added veteran Keenan Allen before the trade deadline. Second-year wideout Jordan Watkins has also taken on a bigger role in part due to Evans’ absence. Watkins has 10 catches for 213 yards and a touchdown in his last four games. The return of Evans comes at the right time as the Niners take on a tough Vikings defense that limited the Green Bay Packers’ explosive offense to just 10 points at Lambeau Field. Packers QB Jordan Love was limited to only 220 yards, his third-lowest total of the season. The 49ers offense has been firing on all cylinders since the bye week, with 74 points scored in wins against the Raiders and Cowboys. Evans’ presence will provide quarterback Brock Purdy with another reliable receiving option in what could be a challenging contest against the Vikings. item.title: Bruno Fernandes confirms Man Utd contract offer but says he’ll leave if it's the right time
item.description: Bruno Fernandes confirms Man Utd contract offer but says he’ll leave if it's the right time Bruno Fernandes has revealed that Manchester United have offered him a new contract, but said he's prepared to leave if all parties decide it's the right time. Fernandes's current contract expires at the end of the season, though United hold an option to extend his deal until 2028. The 32-year-old was named PFA Player of the Year in 2025/26 after breaking the Premier League 's single-season assist record, but has been part of a struggling side this season. United are 19th in the Premier League table ahead of facing Liverpool this afternoon, in what will be Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge. The Argentine has replaced Michael Carrick following the club's worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign. Ahead of that game, Fernandes said he has rejected multiple offers to leave Manchester in recent summers and outlined his commitment to the club. However, he said now is not the time to discuss a new deal with the focus on improving results. "I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester," he said to Sky Sports. "Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on. "I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door. "Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

item.title: Tom Izzo Unloads on NCAA Over Detroit Mercy Punishment
item.description: Michigan State head coach Tom Izzo wasn’t holding back following the Spartans’ 91-70 victory over Detroit Mercy on Saturday afternoon. But his frustration had nothing to do with his team’s performance. Instead, Izzo took aim at the NCAA over its punishment of Detroit Mercy and head coach Mark Montgomery, a former Michigan State player and longtime Izzo assistant. “The APR is a joke,” Izzo said during his postgame press conference . “You can’t have an APR when kids are allowed to leave whenever they want.” Izzo’s frustration stems from penalties handed down to Detroit Mercy after the program failed to meet the NCAA’s Academic Progress Rate (APR) requirements. Those penalties include a postseason ban for the 2026-27 season and restrictions on practice time. Michigan State’s men’s basketball coach Tom Izzo yells during a men’s college basketball game between Tennessee and Michigan State at Thompson-Boling Arena at Food City Center on Nov. 17, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Izzo Defends His Former Assistant Izzo believes Montgomery is being punished for academic problems that developed before he took over the program. He was particularly upset that the sanctions went beyond postseason eligibility and affected how often the Titans could practice. According to Detroit Mercy’s official announcement , the program failed to reach the required APR benchmark of 930. The university acknowledged its academic shortcomings while also questioning whether the current system adequately accounts for today’s transfer-heavy college basketball environment. Izzo’s criticism comes as he has repeatedly questioned the impact of the transfer portal and the NCAA’s approach to regulating college athletics. He has also challenged recent NCAA eligibility decisions . For Izzo, however, Saturday’s criticism was personal. Montgomery played for Michigan State from 1988-92 and later spent years on Izzo’s coaching staff. The Spartans improved to 5-1 with Saturday’s victory, but Izzo made sure the conversation didn’t end with the final score. His former assistant’s situation clearly struck a nerve, and the NCAA was squarely in his sights.

item.title: Key Barcelona star to miss Deportivo clash after red card on the bench vs Villarreal
item.description: Key Barcelona star to miss Deportivo clash after red card on the bench vs Villarreal La Liga giants Barcelona will be forced to make do without the services of a leading member of the club’s midfield ranks in their next domestic outing. item.title: Packers Sign Familiar Face Amid Josh Jacobs Injury Questions
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 18: Pierre Strong Jr. #22 of the Green Bay Packers runs the ball after a catch against Jaishawn Barham #55 of the Dallas Cowboys during the first quarter at Lambeau Field on October 18, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers. Getty Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs returned to practice on Saturday. However, head coach Matt LaFleur does not anticipate Jacobs playing in the team’s Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Rams unless something substantially changes with his finger. As a response, the Packers re-signed veteran running back Pierre Strong to the practice squad. They released edge rusher D.J. Johnson as the corresponding move. Strong has been active for the Packers for five games this season. Green Bay Packers Sign Pierre Strong Back to Practice Squad Getty Head coach Matt LaFleur of the Green Bay Packers. The injuries in the running back room led to Strong having a role early on in the season. Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner’s exempt list, and then shortly after that Chris Brooks was placed on the IR. Because Kaleb Johnson was just acquired in a trade before the season started, he was slow to get onto the field as well. So the team relied on strong early in the season. Strong has mostly been a passing-down weapon, so he only has 25 carries this season, but has 114 snaps played. Despite playing 30 snaps in Week 9, he was a healthy scratch in Week 10 when the team brought Brooks back. Johnson had started to ascend as the lead back and the team still is not giving up on third-round pick MarShawn Lloyd. Beyond that, he is still on his rookie salary, so the team would have to see him clear waivers. Strong is a journeyman who’s been on three teams in five seasons. He was only brought in because the team lacked depth and needed some help. So he was more likely to clear waivers than Lloyd. With Brooks back into the mix, the team did not have a significant need for a strong either, so if he did end up getting claimed on waivers, it would not have been a big loss. Packers Add Strong Back to Practice Squad The news is likely not good for the status of Jacobs playing in Week 11. Green Bay will lean on Johnson, with Lloyd as the backup and Brooks as the third-down back. Adding Strong is depth because they do not plan to have any with Jacobs out. Now that he has re-signed with the team, they can use three practice squad elevations on him before they have to decide to bring him back onto the active roster. If Jacobs is out, they have a chance to use one of them on Strong in Week 12. Releasing Johnson is a good sign that Micah Parsons will be back this week, as the team does not need depth on the edge anymore. Green Bay faces the Rams in Week 12. We will see if Strong gets called up and if Jacobs is active. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Packers Sign Familiar Face Amid Josh Jacobs Injury Questions

item.title: Ohio State’s Ryan Day Buyout, Contract in Focus After Nebraska Loss
item.description: LINCOLN, NEBRASKA - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes stands with the team before the game against the Nebraska Cornhuskers at Memorial Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Lincoln, Nebraska. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes follows gameplay during the first quarter of a game against the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 7: Head Coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes talks with the referees during a timeout in the second quarter of the game against the Oregon Ducks at Ohio Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) Getty The Ohio State Buckeyes have now lost four games this season. That simply doesn’t happen in Columbus, and that means Ryan Day’s job is in jeopardy, even if a buyout of his contract probably remains unlikely. There are certainly some OSU fans who are likely fed up with Day. There are surely others who are giving him a pass this season because starting quarterback Julian Sayin got hurt, and three of Ohio State’s losses have come since then. Either way, it’s been an uglier season than anyone at Ohio State has had to deal with in a long time. They won’t be going to the College Football Playoff. Their last chance to gain some grace will come on Saturday, Nov. 28 when they host archrival Michigan for The Game. A win over the Wolverines will make everything feel a bit better. A loss? Day would be in major trouble if Ohio State doesn’t beat Michigan on Saturday. Ryan Day Contract Details Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO – NOVEMBER 14: Head coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes follows gameplay during the first quarter of a game against the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) Ryan Day’s current contract stems from a seven-year contract extension he signed in February 2025. It runs through the 2031 season, meaning there are five full seasons remaining after 2026. According to CBS Sports , the contract pays Day $12.5 million per year. There are various annual bonuses for titles that can total up to $1.55 million per season, if Day checks all the boxes — spoiler, he won’t be checking all the boxes this season. There’s also a small $250,000 retention bonus that Day can get paid in 2027 if he’s still around. Ryan Day Buyout Details Getty COLUMBUS, OHIO – NOVEMBER 7: Head Coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes talks with the referees during a timeout in the second quarter of the game against the Oregon Ducks at Ohio Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) For Ohio State to buy Ryan Day out of his contract, it would cost $11.5 million times the remaining years on his contract. So with five years left after this one, it would cost $57.5 million for Day to be bought out

item.title: PSG confirm another devastating, season-ending injury to first team star
item.description: PSG confirm another devastating, season-ending injury to first team star PSG have lost another one of their key players to injury, with devastating news about Desire Doue coming out this afternoon. If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. Things have taken a dramatic negative turn for PSG. Desire Doue went off injured against Nice yesterday afternoon, looking in great pain. Today, the club have confirmed everyone’s worst fears – the attack has ruptured the ACL in his right knee. The Parisians were already without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who suffered the same injury a month ago. Losing one world class attacker was bad, but the quality the team have in attack meant it wasn’t an impossible objective. Now, without two of them, the season looks very different. Ligue 1 is still of course likely to be a cruise as it so often is. But the chances of a third consecutive Champions League have dropped precipitously. PSG new arrivals must step up earlier than expected Mika Godts playing for Belgium. (Photo by Marco Rosi/Getty Images) PSG added Mika Godts and Maghnes Akliouche in attack this summer. They were expected to be worked in gradually, but both will now be playing in almost every game now. The pressure is also now on fellow summer arrival Ferran Torres, who has had a quiet spell and will now need to step up to a world class level. In other news… Lucas Digne was left out of the PSG squad to face Nice, another sign of how badly things have gone since his transfer. Luis Enrique has confirmed that Ousmane Dembele is fit to play in today’s game . Reporters claim that Lucas Chevalier has not asked to leave PSG in January, despite rumours to the contrary.

item.title: Real Madrid fans up in arms over goal that sparked Barcelona comeback vs Villarreal
item.description: Real Madrid fans up in arms over goal that sparked Barcelona comeback vs Villarreal Supporters of Real Madrid have on Sunday taken firm aim at the standard of officiating in La Liga. This comes amid claims that arch rivals Barcelona secured a crucial advantage courtesy of a mistake en route to their comeback victory over Villarreal. Hansi Flick’s troops marked their return to action a short time ago, kicking the defence of their Spanish top-flight title back into gear in a meeting with the aforementioned Villarreal. Inside the opening seven minutes, Barcelona found themselves trailing by two goals to nil. A 2nd-half explosion, however, ultimately gave rise to a 3-2 Blaugrana triumph. The Catalans’ comeback was kicked into gear courtesy of a fine Gerard Martín header, at the end of a cleverly worked corner routine. As alluded to above, though, those of a Real Madrid persuasion are adamant that a corner should never have been awarded in the first place. After João Cancelo took aim at goal from distance, the ball crashed off the post and behind. It initially appeared as though the ball had taken a touch on the way through, though replays were more unclear. Real Madrid’s fans, though, appear nothing short of certain that a goal-kick was the correct decision, widely highlighting an unfair advantage gained by their bitter rivals amid the tight La Liga title race: Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Pedri 9, Yamal 9 | Barcelona 3-2 Villarreal: Player Ratings
item.description: Pedri 9, Yamal 9 | Barcelona 3-2 Villarreal: Player Ratings Barcelona returned from the international break and played their first game of the next phase of the season against Villarreal on Sunday afternoon at the Spotify Camp Nou. They began the game completely dominated and overwhelmed by Villarreal’s energy – something they simply could not keep up with. By half-time, they were 2-0 down, and seemed to have no solutions. Hansi Flick made no panic changes even at half-time, and trusted the same XI. They repaid his faith with a great comeback. Goals from Gerard Martin and Fermin Lopez helped Barcelona get level, and an own goal from Pau Navarro helped them get ahead. Eventually, they held on to the lead and saw the game off to earn all three points. Barça Universal brings you the player ratings from Barcelona 3-2 Villarreal. Joan Garcia: 6 Joan Garcia conceded two goals in the opening ten minutes, and while he was indeed let down by the defence, there is a feeling he could have done a bit more. Neither of the two strikes that resulted in goals for Villarreal came from particularly close range, and the goalkeeper looked helpless in both cases. At least one of the two, given Garcia’s calibre, should have been parried away. Joao Cancelo: 6 Cancelo continued to look like a shadow of his former self, as he has in recent games. He did not show much personality going forward, and his link-up play was sub-par. Even his defensive work rate was relatively questionable, and it is high time some questions begin being asked about his regular starter status given his form. Gerard Martin: 7.5 A rare goal for Gerard Martin. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Gerard Martin, as part of the central defence, holds much of the accountability for the two early goals conceded, especially given that he was the only natural centre-back starting. His distribution under the Villarreal press was underwhelming, and his positioning for both of the opposition’s early strikes was poor. Made up for his poor first half with an improved showing after the break and a great goal to open the scoring for Barcelona. Frenkie de Jong: 8 Despite playing out of position, De Jong seemed to contribute more to Barcelona’s stability than the rest of the defence combined as he shone with the ball and helped retain it on a night where the Catalans struggled for order. The Dutchman was confident on the ball and made the right defensive decisions more often than not. Continued to grow into the second half and finished the game as one of the best players on the field. Eric Garcia: 7 Eric Garcia made his return from injury and was decent at right-back, although Villarreal’s second goal did come from a through ball down his wing. He did more than Cancelo in attack, but was still nowhere close to his best. Contributed to Barcelona’s winning goal with a good cross into the area that the Villarreal defence struggled to deal with. Marc Bernal: 6 The academy star was perhaps the single-most disappointing

item.title: Zaire Franklin explains how a “Freak accident” left him with a broken leg
item.description: Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin has been sidelined since October after suffering a shin injury during practice. He has spent the past several weeks working toward a return and rejoined the team on the practice field Saturday. Speaking with reporters afterward, Franklin described the incident as a “freak accident” and detailed how the injury happened, according to ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. “Somebody just kind of kneed me in a weird way. I’m thinking it’s just dead leg. I actually finished practice. I practiced two more periods on a broken leg. And then once I got the X-ray and it was broke, I was looking like, I almost couldn’t believe it. It just looked fake,” Franklin remarked via ESPN’s Rob Demovsky. Zaire Franklin with the Packers Oct 18, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers Kamal Hadden (36) celebrates with Zaire Franklin (44) and Isaiah McDuffie (58) against Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field at Lambeau Field. He made an immediate impression after joining Green Bay this year, but his shin injury has restricted him to six appearances. After spending weeks away from the field, the veteran linebacker is clearly pleased to be back practicing with the team. Oct 11, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin (44) reacts after a play against the Chicago Bears during the second quarter at Lambeau Field. item.title: 2027: Any party saying I’ve stepped down is working for Tinubu - Atiku
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has accused political parties spreading claims that he has withdrawn from the 2027 presidential race of working in favour of President Bola Tinubu. Atiku described the reports as false and insisted that he remained in the contest to win the election. In a statement issued on Sunday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice-president said no group claiming to be his supporters had the authority to announce his withdrawal. “Any party promoting the lie that I have stepped down is doing Tinubu’s work. Every false withdrawal story tries to clear his strongest opponent from the field,” he said. Atiku added that he had not made any decision to leave the race, dismissing claims attributed to individuals presenting themselves as his supporters. “Putting my name on a placard does not make someone my supporter. Putting a lie in that person’s mouth does not make it my decision,” he said. He warned that any attempt to remove him from the contest through fabricated declarations would deny Nigerians the opportunity to choose their preferred candidate. “If I am not on the ballot, Bola Tinubu might as well wait for a coronation. But I am in this race to win, and Nigerians will have their choice,” he said. The former vice-president also accused those behind the reports of using misinformation to weaken the opposition, alleging that the tactic was intended to benefit the ruling All Progressives Congress. He urged opposition parties seeking to defeat Tinubu to focus on persuading voters rather than circulating claims about rival candidates. “Anyone serious about defeating the APC should take their case to voters. Manufacturing supporters and circulating false declarations will not defeat Tinubu. It only serves him,” Atiku said. On his campaign activities, Atiku said his Affordable Life agenda remained focused on addressing the economic difficulties confronting Nigerian households. He cited the rising cost of food and transportation as issues his campaign intended to address, saying the campaign was reaching communities across the country. “Hunger and poverty are not on social media. They are in our markets, our homes and every community where families struggle to afford food and transport,” he said. Atiku urged his supporters to remain mobilised ahead of the election and ensure they had their Permanent Voter Cards. He reiterated that he would not withdraw in favour of any other candidate, declaring that the contest would be decided by voters. “I do not need anyone to step down for me, and I am stepping down for no one,” he said. The statement concluded with Atiku expressing confidence that he would defeat Tinubu at the ballot box on January 16, 2027. The post 2027: Any party saying I’ve stepped down is working for Tinubu - Atiku appeared first on Vanguard News .

Fernandes puts Man Utd contract talks on hold
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes (Glyn KIRK) Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has revealed it is "not the right time" for talks over a new contract with his troubled club. Fernandes's future at Old Trafford has been a source of constant doubt in recent years and the speculation that he is ready to quit United continues to swirl. With his current deal due to expire at the end of the season, the 32-year-old has turned down a second offer of a new contract. Fernandes snubbed the chance to move to Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal in the close-season, but with United in turmoil this term, he is not ready to reopen contract talks with the club he joined in 2020. "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay," Fernandes told Sky Sports on Sunday. "There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. "I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. "Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. "I've always showed how much I care about this club and how much I want to win at this club. I've always said, the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on." The Portugal midfielder's form has dipped this season and he has only managed one goal and assist since his hat-trick against Ipswich in August. Fernandes was dropped by Michael Carrick earlier this season after criticising his tactics. Carrick has since been sacked, with Mauricio Pochettino hired to lift United away from the relegation zone. Often criticised for his emotional outbursts and body language on the pitch, Fernandes is keeping his focus on United's cause for now as they start a new era under former USA coach Pochettino. "We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract," Fernandes said. "But about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations. "The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games." smg/dmc

item.title: Unlikely heroes in TE room fire Michigan Football to upset win bs UCLA
item.description: I don’t believe it. You probably don’t either. But it’s happened. The unranked Michigan football team, mired in a season shaped by disappointment and mockery, has beaten an undefeated, top-five team in the country. The Wolverines stunned No. 4 UCLA, 18-16 in triple overtime. And they did it off the backs of a position group that hasn’t been at its best all year long. Michigan has lacked a tight end capable of shouldering the offense this season for the first time in years. Following the steady play of Marlin Klein and Colston Loveland, the Wolverines rolled out a more ragtag array in 2026, led by Hogan Hansen and Jalen Hoffman. But that group stepped up on Saturday, delivering both of Michigan’s scoring plays in its most stunning victory of the year. “I’ll tell you what, Mason Bonner did some good things tonight as well, and he’s a tight end technically,” head coach Kyle Whittingham said. “He’s played mostly, flexed out in wide receiver … but those guys have been great contributors. Hogan Hansen’s contributed throughout the season as well…” After three relatively tepid quarters, it was Bonner who broke open the scoring. With a clean pocket, Underwood was able to find Bonner right into the end zone to his left, who made a hugely impressive one-handed grab for the score. It was the freshman’s first receiving touchdown of his career, and though a boom-or-bust outing — three grabs for 47 yards and the touchdown — he certainly made a mark. The other tight end to make a mark didn’t actually record a single reception on the stats sheet. Yet his play was the game-winner. With the game into triple overtime and Michigan needing a successful two-point conversion to win, Hoffman, a former walk-on and senior who had recorded zero receptions in his first three seasons, practically ripped the ball out of the defensive back’s hands for the win — a Hollywood moment. “I’m just proud of that room,” Hoffman said. “And we’ve all went through a lot, virtually the whole team’s went through a lot. We kept working, kept fighting, and when opportunities came, we made plays.” All year long, the Wolverines’ tight ends room hasn’t been the crux of the offense. The position group’s statistical leader is Hansen with just 128 yards. Even in a highly dysfunctional year of offense for Michigan, the burden has been shouldered by the receiving room, as injured wideout JJ Buchanan has captured the lions’ share of yards and targets. But that didn’t matter on Saturday — because when Michigan needed help, it got it from two unlikely heroes.

item.description: NORMAN, OKLAHOMA - OCTOBER 31: Quarterback LaNorris Sellers #16 of the South Carolina Gamecocks breaks loose for a 30-yard gain against defensive back Peyton Bowen #22 of the Oklahoma Sooners in the second quarter at Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Norman, Oklahoma. item.title: Antonelli reveals last-lap Vegas mistake that saw him 'smoked' by McLarens
item.description: Kimi Antonelli has admitted his own battery management mistake on the last lap of the Las Vegas Grand Prix "compromised" his chance at victory against Max Verstappen . Hoping to attack the Dutchman on Lap 50 in Sin City, the Italian was instead "smoked by the McLarens" and finished fourth. Despite going quickest in Las Vegas GP Qualifying, Antonelli started the race from P6 after taking a five-place engine penalty, but was fighting for the win in the closing stages of a race featuring a total of 352 overtakes. 35 of those passes were for the lead, and while most were between fierce rivals Verstappen and Antonelli's Mercedes teammate George Russell, the new world champion became the closest challenger to the Red Bull driver with 12 laps to go before Russell's crash at Lap 48 when trying to pass Antonelli. Last-lap battery blunder costs Antonelli Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures With Mercedes and Red Bull working on figuring out the best battery management strategy in anticipation of a last-lap shootout to the line, Antonelli explained where it all went wrong, and how he became vulnerable to McLaren duo Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri behind him. The 20-year-old told Sky F1 : "I think the change of deployment was good because it was the best option to then stay ahead after the chicane in case I was overtaking Max before turn 14. "But because I wanted to keep the overtake mode, I lifted off and reapplied some throttle to keep a little bit of speed, and that messed up the whole battery harvesting, and at the chicane I had zero. "So I lost more than a second going into Turn 1 and, not only couldn't stay close to Max and give myself a good shot for the win, I got smoked by the two McLarens as well and lost the podium. "So probably was a mistake on my side but in the moment it is also very difficult because I thought I was doing something right to stay behind and keep the overtake [mode] but turned it compromised the race." Antonelli reveals last-lap plan to beat Verstappen While he may have been constantly exchanging places with Verstappen towards the closing stages, Antonelli revealed that he had hoped to stay behind the Red Bull driver just prior to the chequered flag. As F1's youngest ever champion explains, the hope was to avoid "forcing anything" and preserve overtake mode for an attack in the final corners. In the end, it was not to be, but the 20-year-old still managed to have some fun during what was an exciting race. "My goal, my objective, was to stay behind all the way to the end," he said. "And as you could see, there was a lot of back and forth between him and me, but I didn't force anything, and I was just trying to stay behind, keep the overtake to give myself the best shot at the end. Especially for the last two straights. "Apart from that, it was a fun race. We were all close to each other. It was a lot of back and forth and a lot of strategy behind it. So, on that side, it required a lot of work. It was just a shame to finish

item.title: This viral star projector has been hyped to Mars and back, but we hunted down the best version you can buy
item.description: It was only a matter of time, but AI has come for astronomy accessories. I’ve yet to see a fictional elderly craftsman begging you to buy his hand-carved telescopes; however, it has absolutely muddied the waters around this viral gooseneck Galaxy Projector Night Light. The good news is that there is an impressive little star projector to be had here, and I’m here to cut through the AI-assisted hype. To make sure you’re not hoodwinked, I’ve done the online legwork to bring you the best version of this device, and it won’t cost you a fortune to put a planetarium in your pocket. Before we dive into what makes this Galaxy Projector Night Light so great, there are a couple of pressing issues to address. No variant of this USB-powered star projector will break up heated dinner arguments by casting a beautifully animated space whale on the ceiling, as one ridiculous AI-generated advert asserts. Its projections are eye-catching enough to entertain space fans young and old, but they’re strictly static. Also, while you might be tempted by the lure of 24 interchangeable slides, compared to this Galaxy Projector Night Light’s 13, this lesser model’s slide selection is a letdown. Not only are the slides smaller and blurrier than this model, a large number are dedicated to seasonal holidays. As much as I enjoy Christmas, if I had Santa’s colossal face gazing down at me from the ceiling I’d never sleep again. Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light review More than meets the eye Aside from the projector itself, the Zanbix 2 in 1 Galaxy Projector Night Light includes 13 swappable slides, crammed into a compact box. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) I tempered my expectations when I first got my hands on the Galaxy Projector Night Light. Packed in a small, relatively unassuming box, it looks remarkably similar to the standard model that’s spread across TikTok, YouTube, Facebook and so on. Just like that one, it’s powered via USB, with a flexible stalk, a slot for slides and a nose-mounted focus wheel. However, once I hooked it up to a handy USB socket, all my reservations vanished, and I was seriously impressed by the power of this little projector. You’ll need a darkened room but the Galaxy Projector Night Light’s larger lens is a serious step-up from the run-of-the-mill version. Its images are richer and clearer than you’d expect from a projector this size, and easily capable of transforming a mid-sized ceiling or wall into a cosmic display. This stunning image of the Pillars of Creation originally came from the James Webb Space Telescope. (Image credit: Chris McMullen) This stunning James Webb Space Telescope image of the Pillars of Creation, with its vast columns of gas and dust, is a perfect example of the projections on offer. The fact the display was static didn’t diminish its wow factor, and I spent a good 15 minutes gazing at it in wonder. The Galaxy Projector Night Light does have a four-hour shut-off in case you drift off or want to use it

item.title: Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29
item.description: The death toll from Friday’s boat accident in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State has risen to 29, with over 50 survivors receiving treatment in hospitals. Governor Douye Diri disclosed this during a condolence visit by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Diri explained that the final casualty figure had yet to be established as efforts were still ongoing to recover the affected vessel. ﻿ He, however, said some passengers might still be trapped inside the boat. The governor described the incident as avoidable, alleging that the boat was not fit for river travel and had operated from an unauthorised loading point. He said the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills and feeding of the survivors. Diri thanked President Tinubu for the concern shown by the Presidency since the incident occurred, particularly the Vice President’s visit to the state. He used the occasion to appeal for Federal Government support for the construction of more roads across Bayelsa, noting that improved road access would reduce the dependence of some communities on water transportation. The accident occurred on Friday, November 20, 2026, when a boat conveying mourners to a burial ceremony capsized near Oweikorogha Community in the Ukubie area of Southern Ijaw. The Bayelsa State Police Command confirmed the incident in a statement, adding that the boat was travelling from Ayama Community to Ukubie for a burial ceremony on Friday, when it capsized at about 11 a.m. The boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways, according to a preliminary police report. Following the incident, rescue operations were launched, with several passengers rescued while others were initially reported missing. A survivor had also alleged that the wooden passenger boat, popularly known as a ‘love boat’, was overloaded with passengers and their belongings. President Bola Tinubu expressed condolences to the families of the victims, describing the incident as tragic and directing relevant federal disaster response agencies to support rescue and recovery efforts. He also approved ₦250 million in support for the families of the victims. The post Death Toll From Bayelsa Boat Accident Rises To 29 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Director Jonathan Frakes reflects on his triumphant time-travel blockbuster (interview)
item.description: null " Star Trek: First Contact " celebrates its 30th anniversary today, and the engaging sci-fi classic still looks fantastic three decades later. With the sad passing of its star, Patrick Stewart , last month, and "Star Trek's" milestone 60th birthday taking place in 2026, this is a bittersweet salute that also holds an extra special significance. Directed by "The Next Generation's" Number One, Jonathan Frakes , in his feature film debut, " First Contact " consistently ranks as one of the finest "Star Trek" feature films among fans and critics, and those accolades are well deserved. Based on a compelling screenplay by Brannon Braga and Ronald D. Moore, "First Contact" remains as bright and beautiful as ever, brimming with bravado, heart, horror, and heroism. Not only was it a bona fide crowdpleaser when it was released by Paramount over Thanksgiving week on Nov. 22, 1996, but it was also a financial success for the studio, eventually pulling in a worldwide total of $212 million off a modest $45 million budget. Honestly, who can forget Alice Krige's seductive Borg Queen, Marina Sirtis’ Deana Troi tipsy on tequila, Brent Spiner's Data feeling the sensation of human skin, Patrick Stewart’s Jean-Luc Picard reliving past traumas, and James Cromwell's Zephram Cochrane blasting off in the Phoenix and dancing to Roy Orbison's "Ooby Dooby"? We caught up with Frakes for "First Contact's" 30th anniversary to hear why this "Trek" treasure holds up and warp back to Hollywood’s heyday of the '90s. Resistance is futile! "What’s not to love?" Frakes tells SPACE regarding the film’s lasting popularity. "It was bulletproof. Dean Devlin ["Stargate," "Independence Day"] and I have very similar sensibilities about filmmaking. We like the whole idea of action, adventure, comedy, and in the case of 'First Contact,' a little horror as well. ILM’s John Knoll, the guy who won the Oscar for 'Star Wars,' just happened to be our Special Effects Supervisor." "Star Trek: First Contact" celebrates its 30th birthday on Nov. 22, 2026. (Image credit: Paramount) "First Contact" is filled with memorable moments and indelible performances, some of which certainly stand out for Frakes looking back over the years on the production. "The two things that always come to mind were the beautiful scene with Alfre [Woodard] and Patrick, the Moby Dick scene, where she says, 'You broke your little ships,'" he recalls. "I was sitting under the camera with my face in my hands, watching two heavyweights go at it take after take. It was what you dream of. They were into it. The writing was great. We had time to do it right, and they were fabulous together. "That and the Cromwell and Marina drunk on tequila scene. It's not only one extended take, but it contributes to the pace of the movie in the right kind of way. My wife tells me that I was really good in that scene because I was exhausted and relaxed. It’s true, you’re exhausted when you’re filming and acting at the same time. I got to sit ther

item.title: On this day in space! Nov.22, 1989: NASA launches space shuttle Discovery on classified STS-33 mission for the US military
item.description: null On Nov. 22, 1989, the space shuttle Discovery launched on the secret mission STS-33 for the U.S. military. It lifted off from Kennedy Space Center and up into the dark of night. This was the third nighttime launch of the shuttle program and the 32nd shuttle mission overall. Discovery had five astronauts on board. Their mission was to deploy a classified payload for the U.S. Department of Defense. NASA and the military launched several secretive shuttle missions to deploy military satellites . The satellite that launched with STS-33 is believed to be a type of spy satellite called Magnum. But exactly what Magnum was doing in orbit remains classified. NASA's space shuttle Discovery launches on the classified STS-33 mission for the U.S. military on Nov. 22, 1989. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered From its start, the Space Transportation System, better known as the space shuttle, was a compromise between meeting civilian and military needs. NASA saw the vehicle as a means of supporting science research, establishing an on-orbit economy (servicing commercial satellites and flying company payloads) and ultimately, assembling the parts for a space station. The Department of Defense saw the shuttle as an asset to deploying and retrieving reconnaissance satellites, among other projects, some of them classified. It was not until the loss of the space shuttle Challenger, that it was decided that the shuttle would only be used by the military when it was key to national security. Other needs would be met by expendable launch vehicles (ELVs). As an aside, the STS-33 astronauts also spent Thanksgiving in space during this mission. But the holiday was off to a crappy start when the shuttle's toilet broke first thing in the morning. After spending most of the day fixing it, they got to enjoy their Thanksgiving turkey together. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Israel investigates West Bank fires
item.description: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank, in attacks local activists say were carried out by Israeli settlers. Around eight vehicles were reportedly torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area. The attacks come amid a surge in settler violence since the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023, with more than 1,100 Palestinians killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers in the West Bank since then, according to an AFP tally. They also follow recent sanctions announced by the UK and Australia against eight Israeli companies involved in settlement activity. France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky shares further details from Jerusalem.

item.title: “Money in a Wheelbarrow”: Adekunle Gold & Blaqbonez Are Making Big-Money Talk Sound Good
item.description: Artwork for Adekunle Gold and Blaqbonez’s collaboration “Money in a Wheelbarrow”. Did you ever envisage an Adekunle Gold and Blaqbonez collaboration? You’re not alone, neither did we, but as it turns out, “ Money in a Wheelbarrow ” is officially here—and Adekunle Gold shared that this is actually a link-up with an artist who released a diss track about him years ago, plus their second attempt at making a song together. If you enjoy a track with a cheeky backstory behind it, this one is all about celebrating your hard-earned bag, enjoying the fruits of your grind and soaking up good moments right now instead of putting joy off until later. On the song itself, Adekunle Gold brings his smooth, melodic touch alongside Blaqbonez’s witty rap delivery as they trade lines about stacking cash, containers landing in Apapa and living large. You get a lively mix of English, Nigerian Pidgin and Yoruba phrasing that makes you want to sing along fast, turning big-money talk into something bright and upbeat rather than heavy. The visuals match that playful mood right from the start, with bold pixel-style lettering flashing across the screen over a bright backdrop where both artists are dressed in sharp dark suits, ties, sunglasses and stacks of cash. Watching them pose around wheelbarrows piled with money as words like “Wheel Barrow”, “Pack Am O”, “Container”, “Apapa”, “Hosana” and “Duffel Bag” pop up gives the video a fun, tongue-in-cheek edge that keeps your eyes locked on the screen. I f you want a fresh, upbeat tune with a funny plot twist behind it, “Money in a Wheelbarrow” is ready for your playlist. *** Photo Credit: Adekunle Gold/Instagram The post “Money in a Wheelbarrow”: Adekunle Gold & Blaqbonez Are Making Big-Money Talk Sound Good appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: It Will Be Difficult To Stabilise What Tinubu Has Done If We Don’t Re-Elect Him — Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that denying President Bola Tinubu a second term will amount to abandoning and undermining the positive effects of the various economic reforms and other policies his administration has started to implement. ﻿ Wike argued that though the removal of fuel subsidy came with initial difficulties, it would be in the best interest of Nigeria and its people for the President to complete the foundation he has laid for the country’s recovery and prosperity. He spoke on Sunday during a thanksgiving and dedication service at St. Peter’s Anglican Church, Rumueprikom, his hometown in Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, where the Rainbow Coalition campaign council was dedicated ahead of the 2027 general elections. Wike Wike, who said the campaigns would begin on November 23, described Tinubu as a courageous leader who took difficult decisions to prevent Nigeria from collapsing. “This country was on the verge of collapse, on the verge of collapse, but by the grace of God, He gave us somebody who is courageous,” the former governor said. The minister cited the relative stability in the university system, saying lecturers’ strikes over unpaid entitlements, which previously disrupted academic calendars, are no longer a recurring problem under the Tinubu administration. He also recalled the difficulties pensioners faced in securing their payments, arguing that the President’s decisions were necessary to address the country’s challenges. Wike described the removal of the fuel subsidy as one such difficult decision, acknowledging it came with disadvantages but insisting the challenges were temporary. “Now, in doing that, there must be some disadvantages. “And that’s why they say these disadvantages will be temporarily seen. As he has laid his foundation, now it’s time for prosperity,” he said. “If we don’t re-elect him, then it will be difficult to stabilise what he has done,” he said. The minister called on Christians, Muslims and traditional worshippers to support the re-election bid, insisting that the campaign would not discriminate on religious grounds. “I am not a native doctor, but I need their votes now. I need everybody’s votes because I know they are registered voters,” he added. “The Muslims, I need their votes too. The Christians like you, we need your votes.” Wike also defended the Tinubu administration against claims of religious imbalance in its appointments, saying Christians benefited more from the government than under previous administrations. “Since Nigeria was created, we have never had the kind of appointments that are going on in this country now,” said the minister. He further urged the congregation to participate actively in the forthcoming elections, warning that those who refuse to vote would have to live with the consequences of decisions made by others. “If you don’t participate, and you have a bad leader, it will also affect you,” he added. item.title: 2027: Atiku’s ally dismisses Fubara’s 3m votes pledge to Tinubu
item.description: …Insists Rivers is nobody’s political inheritance, says APC must be punished for emergency rule By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and close ally of its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, Chief Eze Chukwuemeka Eze, has dismissed Governor Siminalayi Fubara’s pledge to deliver three million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general election. Eze described the governor’s assurance as an unrealistic political projection, insisting that Rivers State was not the political inheritance of any individual or group. Fubara had, on November 7, during a Rainbow Coalition/APC presidential rally in Port Harcourt, assured Tinubu that the people of Rivers would deliver at least three million votes for him in the January 2027 presidential election. Reacting to the pledge in a statement issued in Port Harcourt at the weekend, Eze described it as an “audacious exercise in political delusion, electoral deception and monumental grandstanding”. He argued that the projection was unattainable and disconnected from the prevailing political realities in the state, alleging that the governor made the promise to massage the President’s ego and create an impression of widespread political acceptance. The ADC chieftain said Tinubu’s reliance on political assurances from Fubara and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, showed a misunderstanding of the political consciousness of Rivers people and their grievances over the political crisis that engulfed the state. Eze recalled the declaration of a state of emergency in Rivers, the suspension of the governor, his deputy and members of the State House of Assembly, insisting that the people had neither forgotten nor forgiven the circumstances surrounding the intervention. He said Rivers people were politically enlightened enough to distinguish genuine leadership from political manoeuvring and would not surrender their electoral choices to intimidation, patronage or political inducements. “It is rather amusing that President Tinubu appears to have mistaken political silence for political acquiescence and the orchestrated jubilation at Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium for an irrevocable endorsement of his administration,” he said. Eze also cautioned against interpreting the crowd at the APC rally as an indication of the President’s electoral strength in the state. “Let nobody deceive the President with the political theatrics of Nyesom Wike, Governor Siminalayi Fubara and their respective political establishments. “The crowd assembled at the stadium, regardless of its numerical appearance, cannot be substituted for the electorate. A rented or politically mobilised crowd, no matter how imposing, does not constitute an electoral mandate,” he said. He further predicted that Tinubu would struggle to secure 100,000 genuine votes in Rivers in 2027, adding that even such a figure would not necessarily amount to an endorsement of his administration. item.title: Atiku’s aide challenges Tinubu over prosperity promise
item.description: A media aide to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has challenged President Bola Tinubu to provide evidence of economic improvements under his administration, saying Nigerians need tangible results rather than assurances of future prosperity. Ibe made the remarks in a post on his X handle on Sunday while reacting to Tinubu’s message in Ibadan that Nigeria was on the path to prosperity. He argued that Nigerians needed to see improvements in their living conditions, particularly in the cost of food, transportation, electricity and other essential services. According to him, the President should explain the achievements of his administration and how its policies have translated into better living conditions for citizens, especially as he seeks another term in 2027. Ibe questioned how long households would have to contend with rising living expenses, while workers struggle with increasing costs and businesses face energy-related challenges. He maintained that government claims of economic progress should be assessed against the everyday experiences of Nigerians. On the reported agreement to reopen a vehicle assembly plant, Ibe said productive investment was welcome but argued that its benefits should be measured by the actual resumption of operations, employment opportunities and wider economic impact. He also acknowledged the importance of infrastructure development, while stressing that government should equally account for its impact on the livelihoods of citizens. Ibe further questioned the emphasis on future generations in the President’s appeal for Nigerians to remain committed to the administration’s policies, saying the immediate needs of children and struggling households should also receive attention. He called on the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a clear account of the outcomes of the sacrifices associated with its policies, including the benefits recorded and when households could expect meaningful relief. Reacting to Tinubu’s remarks about the opposition, Ibe said opposition parties had a legitimate role in scrutinising the administration’s performance, while citizens were entitled to consider alternative political positions. He argued that public confidence in government should be strengthened through responses to citizens’ concerns and demonstrable improvements in their living conditions. Ibe said the benefits of prosperity should be reflected in household purchasing power, workers’ wages, the survival of businesses and the security of communities. He maintained that the administration should provide evidence of its achievements and address the economic and security concerns confronting Nigerians.
